original_hook: When an asset clears a range on an aggressive liquidity sweep, chasing the wick is a trap—the retest anchor is where the real signal lives. $ZEC expanded out of its $1108–$1250 consolidation base to hit $1385.65 on 99,979 ZEC of 1H volume. Volume immediately contracted by 97% down to 2,572 ZEC as price settled back around $1297. That steep volume collapse confirms overhead market buy orders were filled, leaving price drifting back to test whether the $1250–$1270 breakout zone can convert into structural support. 📊 ZEC 1H: price $1296.66 • support $1098.88 • resistance $1385.65 • TP1 $1457.3425 • target $1529.035 • SL / invalidation $1098.88 (long bias). Levels are chart-derived scenarios, not guarantees. If buyers defend $1250 and reclaim a 1H close above $1336 on rising volume, trend structure remains intact. What confirmation on $ZEC would make you treat this setup as real rather than an early headline move?
